# rgeomex <img src="man/figures/logo.png" align="right" height="139" alt="" />

<!-- badges: start -->
[![r-universe](https://fdzul.r-universe.dev/badges/rgeomex)](https://fdzul.r-universe.dev/rgeomex)
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/fdzul/rgeomex/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/fdzul/rgeomex/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

**English** | [Español](README.es.md)

rgeomex provides the geographic boundaries of Mexico from [INEGI](https://www.inegi.org.mx/temas/mg) and [INE](https://pautas.ine.mx/transparencia/mapas/) at several resolutions (states, municipalities, localities, urban AGEB, blocks and electoral sections), and functions to extract the AGEB, blocks and sections of a locality.

rgeomex is part of the [dengueverse](https://fdzul.github.io/dengueverse/). Its Python version is [rgeomex-py](https://fdzul.github.io/rgeomex-py/); both use the same files.

## Installation

``` r
install.packages("rgeomex",
                 repos = c("https://fdzul.r-universe.dev",
                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

# or from GitHub
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pkg_install("fdzul/rgeomex")
```

## Data

Since version 0.2.0 the datasets are not shipped inside the package. They are GeoParquet files that are downloaded the first time they are used and kept in a local cache (`rgeomex_cache_dir()`), so the installation is small and only the states you use are downloaded. The names of the previous versions still work (for example `rgeomex::AGEM_inegi19_mx`).

| Dataset | Content | Source |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `AGEE_inegi19_mx` | states | INEGI 2019 |
| `AGEM_inegi19_mx`, `AGEM_inegi25_mx` | municipalities | INEGI 2019, 2025 |
| `loc_inegi19_mx` | urban localities | INEGI 2019 |
| `AGEB_inegi_2019` | urban AGEB (by state) | INEGI 2019 |
| `blocks_ine20_mx` | blocks (by state) | INE 2020 |
| `blocks_ine20_mx_centroid` | centroids of the blocks (by state) | INE 2020 |
| `sectores_ine20_mx` | electoral sections (by state) | INE 2020 |
| `hrl_mx`, `pua_mx`, `ua_mx` | other urban boundaries | INEGI |
| `iter_2020_loc` | population of the localities (table) | INEGI 2020 |

## Example

```{r example}
library(rgeomex)

# boundary of a locality
merida <- extract_locality(cve_edo = "31", locality = "Merida")

# AGEB, blocks and electoral sections of a locality
ageb     <- extract_ageb(cve_edo = "31", locality = "Merida")
blocks   <- extract_blocks(cve_edo = "31", locality = "Merida")
sections <- extract_sectores(cve_edo = "31", locality = "Merida")

# a whole dataset, or the rows of some states
rgeomex_datasets()
yucatan <- rgeomex_load("AGEM_inegi19_mx", cve_edo = "31")
```

To work offline, or to share the files among several users, set the environment variable `RGEOMEX_DATA_DIR` to a folder that has the files.

## Credits

The original shapefiles are created by official government institutions ([INEGI](https://www.inegi.org.mx/temas/mg) and [INE](https://pautas.ine.mx/transparencia/mapas/)).
